text:
dmitri: heads up — saw a cluster of SSE 5xxs around the route swap at ~10:02. tracing shows `connection_state=LINGER` and duplicated billing markers in fanout logs.
jen: ugh. can you paste the log snippet? :eyes:
dmitri: sure — here's the relevant line:
```
log: ts=2799998888 conn=abc123 state=LINGER route=proxy-eu-2 fanout_count=2 markers=[bill:tx:451,bill:tx:451] resume_token=rtk-9a1
```
carla: that looks like the fanout wrote the same billing marker twice when the route swap overlapped with an in-flight resume. could be replay + linger window.
mike: is this the case where proxy A forwarded to B while B still had the old partially-closed session? we saw something similar in canary but assumed rate-limiter duplicate suppression would catch it.
dmitri: yeah, proxies appear to be forwarding then also keeping a LINGER connection open for ~15s. clients that reconnect inside that window get both streams, which yields duplicate markers. telemetry doesn't currently dedupe markers, so console shows doubled cost spikes.
ben: so two problems: (1) actual double-increment in billing markers, (2) console/telemetry doesn't surface "duplicate" as a separate signal. agree?
alice: agree. we should avoid changing billing counting semantics in prod rush, but we can add a dedupe layer in telemetry pipeline first to avoid noisy spikes in console.
ryan: can we rely on resume tokens to de-duplicate? if resume_token present, server could tag markers with `resume_epoch` and clients/server could ignore repeated epoch numbers.
jen: resume_token is per-connection and doesn't survive route swaps consistently today. proxies don't always rewrite or preserve that header. that's the root.
carla: proposal: add short-lived `stream-instance-id` header generated at connection time. fanout writes (instance, marker-id). downstream dedupe on (instance, marker-id) for billing/telemetry. cheap and backward-compatible.
mike: that would require a small proxy change to attach `X-Stream-Instance`. doable. do we have a plan for rollouts? if old proxies don't inject it, we still get duplicates but can phase it in.
dmitri: also proposing console UX tweak: when doing route swap rollouts, show "streaming fanout overlap" warning with count of connections in LINGER. gives SREs signal without panicking on immediate billing spike.
ben: +1. separate alerts: one for raw-billing-markers surge, one for deduped-billing surge — helps identity dupes.
jen: ops-bot, can you add a runbook item? quick checklist: detect duplicate markers, verify resume token propagation, add proxy change ticket, and patch telemetry dedupe.
ops-bot: created #inc-279999 for investigation and added initial checklist to runbook.
deploy-bot: rolling out proxy patch to canary (proxy-eu-2) at 10:18. monitor `streaming.fanout.duplicate_count` metric. :rocket:
carla: for the dedupe window, propose 30s TTL for seen (instance, marker) pairs. should cover linger without persistent state.
alice: ok, team plan: (1) telemetry dedupe + console spike smoothing (hotfix), (2) proxy header inject (canary -> gradual), (3) refine resume propagation tests in integration harness. owners: jen (telemetry), mike (proxy), carla (console).
ryan: one more ask: add a lightweight integration test that simulates route-swap with overlapping fanout and asserts markers are idempotent after dedupe. if it flakes, we iterate on TTL.
dmitri: thanks — I'll add the failing log links to the incident ticket and attach pcap. :thumbsup:
ben: nice triage. tagging for postmortem if billing variance > 2x for any customer.
alice: feel free to ping me for dashboard tweaks. I can add a special rollout view showing LINGER counts and deduped vs raw billing.
dmitri: cool. I'll follow-up with exact trace ids.
